findings.reason: The protected app-local and Accepted native sources implement the direct BST split-point search: move left when both targets are smaller, right when both are larger, and otherwise return the current node. The O(h)-time/O(1)-space implementation is concise, conventional, and interview-ready, so no candidate is justified.

The app-local function and native class method have identical current-node initialization, strict same-side comparisons, child transitions, and split return. The app-local TreeNode class is the required standalone equivalent of LeetCode's injected model.

The legal 15/63/255-node balanced BST tiers keep both targets in the deepest left region, binding the protected source to tree height while exposing full-tree work. The protected source passes at -0.00 relative exponent; a correct general-tree parent-map implementation passes every output and fails only scaling at +0.61 with a 9.50x largest runtime ratio.

The Approach correctly proves that each skipped ancestor contains both targets in one proper child and that the first split or equality is therefore lowest. The summary is now problem-specific, and ancestor-target and target-order boundaries are labeled separately.
